The lab was cold on purpose, and Priya had stopped noticing her breath in the air hours ago. On the bench in front of her the instrument hummed, a gleaming cylinder wrapped in tubing and wire, and the display flickered through its warm-up sequence. She had waited two years for this part. When the counter finally ticked over to a stable reading, she let out a long breath and wrote the time in her notebook: 11:42. It worked. Not perfectly, since there was still a drift in the baseline that she would have to chase down in the morning, but it worked. She leaned back on the stool and looked at the little line on the screen, steady and unremarkable, and felt something close to joy.
